resolutions.researcher_notes: Wikipedia (live, fetched directly): 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline (TGPL) is a set of natural gas pipelines that run from the Texas and Louisiana coast... It is one of the largest pipeline systems in the United States' -- present tense, no cessation/abandonment mentioned, and the article's own Expansion-projects section describes ongoing 2014-era investment. Kinder Morgan's own current Natural-Gas operations index page (live, fetched directly): 'Kinder Morgan's Tennessee Gas Pipeline (TGP) is an approximately 11,824-mile pipeline system that transports natural gas...' -- also present tense, listed among KM's currently-operated pipeline assets. Two distinct publishers (Wikipedia, Kinder Morgan) both describe TGP as a presently active system -> supports 'operating', high/independent. Neither uses the literal word 'operating'; this is a present-tense/no-retirement inference, consistent with this cohort's calibration for company/encyclopedia overview pages.

Wikipedia infobox: 'General information / Type: Natural gas'. Kinder Morgan's page: '...Tennessee Gas Pipeline (TGP) is an approximately 11,824-mile pipeline system that transports natural gas...'. Two distinct publishers explicitly identify this as a natural-gas pipeline -> matches sheet's Fuel='Gas', high/independent.

Wikipedia's Expansion-projects section, describing the proposed Northeast Energy Direct branch of this same TGP system, characterizes it in the encyclopedia's own voice as 'a high-volume, high-pressure gas transmission pipeline' -- an explicit 'transmission' classification, though the sentence is framed around safety concerns for the NED branch specifically rather than a blanket statement about the entire historic mainline. No second, independently-worded source explicitly using the word 'transmission' for TGP was located (Kinder Morgan's own overview page never uses the word for TGP specifically, unlike several sibling KM systems that are literally named '___ Gas Transmission'; a JS-rendered PHMSA operator-report page for operator ID 19160 was fetched but returned only generic boilerplate with no TGP-specific text in its static HTML, so it could not be verified as containing the value and is not proposed as a citation). Single source -> medium/independent:false. The classification is also consistent with basic pipeline-engineering usage (a large-diameter, long-distance interstate gas mainline is by definition a transmission line, as opposed to gathering or distribution), but that inference alone is not cited here.

Wikipedia infobox: 'Commissioned 1943' -- exact match to the sheet's StartYear1=1943. Body text confirms: 'The first pipeline was constructed by Tennessee Gas Transmission Company (TGT) beginning in 1943.' This is corroborated in kind by one of the row's own seed citations, a Newspapers.com article headlined 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline Work is Now Under Way' (not independently re-verified here -- newspapers.com requires a paid/login wall that this environment could not get past -- so it is not proposed as a citation, only noted as consistent). Kinder Morgan's current overview page gives no start/history date at all. Only ONE fully-verified, fetchable source (Wikipedia) found for this specific year -> medium/independent:false per the brief's one-source rule.

CONCERN: no source located gives 1,000.00 MMcf/d as a capacity figure for Tennessee Gas Pipeline, and the figures that ARE available describe a system roughly an order of magnitude larger. Kinder Morgan's 2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, fetched directly with a compliant SEC User-Agent), Natural Gas Pipelines segment asset table, as of Dec. 31, 2018: 'TGP 11,775 [miles] 12.10 [Bcf/d Design Capacity] 76 [Bcf storage] -- Marcellus, Utica, Gulf Coast, Haynesville, and Eagle Ford shale supply basins; Northeast, Southeast U.S., Gulf Coast and U.S.-Mexico border.' 12.10 Bcf/d = 12,100 MMcf/d, roughly 12x the sheet's 1,000.00 MMcf/d. EIA's Major Pipeline Summary dataset (State-to-State Capacity, Jan 2023 vintage, checked directly) lists 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co' as ~40 individual interstate segments ranging from 125 to 2,771 MMcf/d (e.g., Gulf Coast Line northward max 2,771 MMcf/d, Texas-Mexico segment 888 MMcf/d, New York-Massachusetts segment 1,169 MMcf/d) -- none of these segment-level figures is exactly 1,000 MMcf/d either, though several are in the same order of magnitude. Neither the system-wide 10-K figure nor any individual EIA segment cleanly matches the sheet's value, so nothing found actually supports 1,000.00 MMcf/d specifically. Since the sheet's Length (11,760 mi) and Start (1943) both correspond to the WHOLE historic TGP mainline system (matching the 10-K's 11,775-mile whole-system figure almost exactly), while Capacity=1,000 MMcf/d is far below that whole system's current 12.10 Bcf/d design capacity, this looks like either (a) a stale/superseded historical capacity figure from an early expansion stage, (b) a single-segment or single-lateral figure mistakenly carried on the row representing the whole system, or (c) a data-entry/units defect. Not changing the value per the no-value-change rule; flagging for Update to investigate against FERC eLibrary docket history (not accessible from this environment) for TGP's original or an intermediate certificated capacity near 1,000 MMcf/d.

Three distinct publishers give closely-clustered whole-system mileage, all within ~1.2% of the sheet's 11,760.00 mi: Wikipedia infobox 'Length 11,900 mi (19,200 km)'; Kinder Morgan's own current overview page 'an approximately 11,824-mile pipeline system'; Kinder Morgan's 2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR) asset table 'TGP 11,775 [miles]' as of Dec. 31, 2018. (KM's website and its own 10-K are the same ultimate publisher, so this counts as one origin plus Wikipedia as the second, independent origin -- still sufficient for the >=2-distinct-publishers bar.) All cluster tightly around 11,760-11,900 miles for the same whole-system asset -> high/independent.

Wikipedia infobox: 'General direction North-east / From Texas-Louisiana Gulf Coast / To New England' -- body text: 'a set of natural gas pipelines that run from the Texas and Louisiana coast through Arkansas, Mississippi, Alabama, Tennessee, Kentucky, Ohio, and Pennsylvania to deliver natural gas in West Virginia, New Jersey, New York, and New England.' Kinder Morgan's page: 'transports natural gas supplied from the Northeast section of the United States, to diverse end-use demand markets including New York City and Boston in the Northeast, the Louisiana and Texas Gulf Coast, and Mexico' (KM's phrasing reflects TGP's modern bidirectional/reversed-flow operation, but names the same Texas-Gulf-Coast <-> Northeast/New England corridor). Both distinct publishers confirm the sheet's StartState/Province=Texas as one end of the system -> high/independent for the Texas endpoint. Per the task instructions, the sheet's EndState/Province cell ('New United Kingdom') is a known find-replace corruption of 'New England' and is not being treated as a research finding here -- for the record, both sources independently corroborate that the intended value IS 'New England' (Wikipedia's infobox literally states 'To New England'), consistent with the already-logged explanation, not a new discovery.

Wikipedia: 'The 11,900-mile (19,200 km) long system is operated by the Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, a subsidiary of Kinder Morgan.' Kinder Morgan's own page names the asset 'Kinder Morgan's Tennessee Gas Pipeline (TGP)' throughout, i.e., operated under the Tennessee Gas Pipeline corporate name within KM's portfolio. Both distinct publishers name 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company' as operator, matching the sheet's 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline LLC' (the LLC designation is the current legal form of the same entity per Kinder Morgan's 2018 10-K, which repeatedly refers to 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C. (TGP)') -> high/independent.

Wikipedia infobox: 'Owner: Kinder Morgan' -- and body text traces the ownership chain: 'In 1996, TGT-owner Tenneco Energy was acquired by El Paso Corporation, which was in turn acquired by Kinder Morgan in 2012,' confirming sole current ownership. Kinder Morgan's own overview page: 'Kinder Morgan's Tennessee Gas Pipeline (TGP)...' -- lists it as a wholly-owned KM asset with no other owner named (KM's 2018 10-K confirms TGP as a consolidated wholly-owned subsidiary, L.L.C.). Two distinct publishers agree Kinder Morgan is the sole owner, matching the sheet's Owner1=Kinder Morgan/100.00% -> high/independent.
